capability: Checkout: the step in which the buyer completes the order (Shopify Checkout, Shopify's checkout settings; Salla Checkout / store-checkout, Guest checkout, Checkout APIs)
note: Parent of CM-CHK-002 to CM-CHK-004. Q1's M-021, a difference of grain: Shopify splits cart (SH-C-046) from checkout (SH-C-047); Salla keeps them in one concern (SA-C-100), which lands here, the coarser capability. Both platforms give checkout a place of its own: Shopify's settings page Checkout and its route checkout-settings (SH-S-1489, SH-S-5106); Salla's dashboard link Checkout at /checkout and its Merchant docs collection Checkout APIs (SA-S-1685, SA-S-1166). Salla's guest checkout (its settings page checkout/guest-checkout and the flag guest-checkout) stays here, under Salla's own checkout settings; WooCommerce's guest-checkout setting is cited in domain D's CM-CUS-010 (customer accounts), see notes. Shopify's Universal Commerce Protocol checkout (dev.ucp.shopping.checkout) is domain F's CM-AIA-005, agentic commerce.

capability: Cart: the buyer's cart before checkout (Shopify Cart, carts/create, Add-to-cart limit; Salla Cart, Cart Items in the Checkout APIs)
note: Under CM-CHK-001 by Salla's grouping: its Checkout APIs collection is "designed for developers building integrations that need to control cart and checkout-entry flows" (SA-S-5139), and its folders Cart and Cart Items sit in that collection (a reading: the collection's sidebar, read as context in observed-sa, not cited). Shopify's own grouping keeps Cart apart from Checkout (its Cart label and carts webhook topics, SH-S-0771, SH-S-6066), so the groupings differ and Salla's is followed, as the one that groups them (notes). The storefront's cart API as such is domain E's (CM-SFR-011, CM-SFR-012); this capability is the cart object and its rules.

capability: Checkout customization and branding: the merchant's editor and settings for the checkout's look and configuration (Shopify Checkout branding, Checkout and accounts configurations, checkout and accounts editor, Checkout customization)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-CHK-001 by Shopify's own route, settings/checkout/editor (SH-S-5103), inside its checkout settings. Shopify's editor configures the checkout and the customer accounts pages together (SH-S-5942); customer accounts themselves are domain D's CM-CUS-010.

capability: Checkout UI extensions: apps' blocks and pages in the checkout and the thank-you page (Shopify Checkout UI, Post-purchase UI, Checkout Extensibility)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-CHK-001 by Shopify's own words, "To augment Shopify checkout with new functionality, build an app with extensions" (SH-S-0679), and its legal heading 9.13 Shopify Checkout Extensibility, "use extensions to customize your checkout" (SH-S-0069). Q1's M-022 joins it to WooCommerce's WC-C-087, for the WooCommerce part. Like D's CM-CUS-014 (customer account UI extensions) and E's CM-POS-004 (POS extensions), the extension surface of one feature stays with the feature; apps as such are domain F's.

capability: Cart and checkout validation: app-written rules that block a cart or checkout from going ahead (Shopify Cart and Checkout Validation, a Shopify Function API)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. No parent: Shopify groups it among its Function APIs (SH-S-0853), not under its checkout or cart. Functions as such are domain F's CM-APP-005, whose note leaves the single features' function APIs to their domains. What a validation checks is not defined in a statement held, beyond its name.

capability: Cart transform: app-written logic that changes the lines of a cart (Shopify Cart Transform, cart transformer, a Shopify Function API)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. No parent: Shopify groups it among its Function APIs (SH-S-0854, SH-S-2225). What a transform does is not defined in a statement held beyond its name; one guide that requests its scope is a bundles guide (SH-S-6173's source page, read as context), which domain B's CM-SEL-006 holds as bundles, not this.

capability: Abandoned checkouts and abandoned carts: the store's records of checkouts and carts the buyer did not complete (Shopify Abandoned checkouts; Salla Abandoned Carts / السلات المتروكة)
note: Q1's unclear candidate U-001, ruled joined here: both platforms give the records a place of their own, Shopify's admin route at checkouts with the permission MANAGE_ABANDONED_CHECKOUTS (SH-S-5001, SH-S-5002), Salla's dashboard app at /marketing/carts and its Merchant API folder Abandoned Carts (SA-S-3591, SA-S-1035). The recovery, the messages and offers that bring the buyer back, is domain D's CM-MKT-022, which cites the recovery statements of the same concerns (SH-S-7224, SH-S-7041, SH-S-5277, SA-S-2099, SA-S-1814, SA-S-1191). Homonym kept in view: Shopify's checkout against Salla's cart, see notes. No parent: Shopify's staff permission puts it under Orders (Orders > Abandoned checkouts), Salla's link under marketing.

capability: Quick checkout: a button or link that shortens the buyer's way through checkout (Salla Quick checkout / زر الشراء السريع, الطلب المباشر, salla-quick-buy; Shopify accelerated checkout buttons)
note: A join on role, a reading: Salla's quick purchase "relies on reducing and speeding up the steps of completing the order" (SA-S-5027); Shopify's accelerated or express checkouts let "returning customers ... more quickly complete payment for their orders" (SH-S-7287), with buttons on Shopify Checkout (SH-S-0419). Shopify's statements are SH-C-078's (PAY batch 4), and Shop Pay (SH-C-074) is the other side of U-026: see notes. Salla's own lines name two things, the quick-buy button (زر الشراء السريع, quick-purchase, salla-quick-buy) and direct ordering (الطلب المباشر, quick-checkout, the route /marketing/quick_checkout); neither is defined apart, so they stay in one capability. No parent: Salla's grouping is marketing, Shopify's is its checkout.

capability: Order options and custom fields at checkout: options and fields the merchant adds for the buyer to fill in when ordering (Salla Cart options / خيارات الطلب, Order Options, Custom fields / حقول مخصصة للطلبات)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Salla's dashboard links Cart options (/orders/options) and Custom fields (/orders/custom-fields) sit in its Orders section (SA-S-1782, SA-S-1780). No parent here: Salla's grouping is its orders section, whose capabilities are batch 2's (ORD). Q1's unclear candidate U-005 sets Shopify's metafields (SH-C-028, domain E) against it: ruled apart. What a cart option is is not defined in a statement held. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping, convention 6: its links are /orders/options and /orders/custom-fields, in the same admin list as All orders (the coordinator, after batch 2).

capability: Orders: the store's orders and their management in the admin (Shopify Orders; Salla Orders / الطلبات, All orders)
note: Parent of CM-ORD-002 to CM-ORD-005, CM-ORD-007, CM-ORD-008 and CM-ORD-010 to CM-ORD-014. Q1's M-023, a difference of grain: Shopify keeps cancellation in orders and splits editing (SH-C-056); Salla splits statuses (SA-C-041) and cancellation (SA-C-046) and keeps editing, manual orders, tags, deleted orders, notes and reorder in SA-C-040. Both coarse concerns (SH-C-054, SA-C-040) land here, and each finer thing is a child. The children follow the platforms' shared grouping: Shopify's routes for editing and creating orders sit in its section Orders (SH-S-7095, SH-S-7094), and Salla's links and settings sit under its Orders section (/orders/...).

capability: Order editing: changing an order after it is placed, and the buyer's requests to edit it (Shopify Edit orders, order edits, requested order edits; Salla Order editing / تعديل الطلب)
note: Under CM-ORD-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's route order:edit is in its section Orders (SH-S-7095); Salla's setting Order editing is orders/edit-policy (SA-S-1747). Q1's M-023 holds SH-C-056 with SA-C-040, which lands in the parent.

capability: Order statuses: the stages an order is set to, which the merchant can customize (Salla Order statuses / حالات الطلب, تخصيص حالات الطلب, Order Status, order.status.updated)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (/orders/statuses, SA-S-1775). Homonym: Shopify's order-status targets (customer-account.order-status.*) are the buyer's order status page in the customer account, not statuses an order is set to (domain D's CM-CUS-014); they are not cited.

capability: Order cancellation (Salla Order cancellation / إلغاء طلب, order.cancelled; Shopify Orders > Cancel, CANCEL_ORDERS, orders/cancelled)
note: Salla gives it a settings page of its own (orders/cancellation, SA-S-1745) and a concern (SA-C-046); Shopify keeps it in SH-C-054 (M-023's granularity), with a staff permission and a webhook topic of its own. Under CM-ORD-001 by both: Shopify's permission is Orders > Cancel; Salla's setting is under orders.

capability: Orders the merchant creates: draft orders and manual orders (Shopify Draft orders, Drafts, Create order; Salla إنشاء طلب يدوي, order_create / إضافة طلب)
note: A join on role, a reading: Shopify's route titled Create order is its draft orders' new route (draftOrders:new, SH-S-7094), and Salla's plan line is إنشاء طلب يدوي, create a manual order (SA-S-1989), with the staff permission order_create (SA-S-2273). Whether Salla's manual order passes through a draft stage, and whether Shopify's drafts serve quotes, isn't stated. Salla's price-quote status (طلب عرض سعر) is domain D's CM-B2B-004. Under CM-ORD-001: Shopify's route is in its section Orders; Salla's plan line is in its group إدارة الطلبات (adar-altlbat).

capability: Order risk and fraud analysis: the platform flags orders that may be fraudulent for the merchant to review (Shopify Built-in fraud analysis, Risk, orders/risk_assessment_changed; Salla نظام الحماية من الاحتيال)
note: No parent: Shopify's help places fraud analysis under managing orders (SH-S-0747), while Salla's plan line sits in its payment group (aldfaa, SA-S-1971). Salla's side is SA-C-122, which scope.tsv gives the PAY area's batch to land (notes). Domain D's CM-CUS-006 holds Salla's tag عميل غير جاد, which rests on the same anti-fraud system (SA-S-5052).

capability: Order assignment to staff (Salla Order Assignment, Auto assignment / إسناد الطلبات تلقائيًا للموظفين)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (/orders/auto-assignee, SA-S-1777). Not Shopify's order routing, which assigns orders to fulfillment locations (SH-C-060, the SHP area).

capability: Order invoices: the invoice the store issues and prints for an order (Salla Order Invoice, Invoice settings / إعداد إصدار فواتير الطلبات, طباعة فاتورة الطلب; Shopify Invoice and receipt apps)
note: A join on role, a reading (U-019): Salla's invoice settings at /orders/invoice-settings and its Order Invoice API, against Shopify's App Store category Invoice and receipt apps, which "offer additional document types" (SH-S-7225). Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping. Homonym: Shopify's draft orders "send invoices" (SH-S-7225), a draft order's invoice to the buyer, not an issued sales invoice. ZATCA e-invoicing is split from SA-C-044 and is the TAX area's.

capability: Packing slips and other printed order documents (Shopify packing slip template, document templates; Salla طباعة ملخص الطلب, order-summary)
note: No parent: Shopify places its packing slip and document template routes in its section Shipping (SH-S-7100, SH-S-7101), and Salla's print order summary sits in its group إدارة الطلبات (SA-S-1988). The SHP area's batch may want it under a fulfilment capability. The admin print action (admin_print), through which apps print documents, is domain F's CM-APP-008. Parent CM-SHP-001 (the coordinator, after batch 11, by convention 6): Shopify's packing slip routes sit in its admin section Shipping (SH-S-7100); Salla's print order summary is a plan line in its order-management group (SA-S-1988), not an admin grouping, so no grouping is shared and Shopify's admin grouping decides.

capability: Order receiving settings: whether, when and how many orders the store accepts, and how a placed order is confirmed (Salla Accept orders / استقبال الطلبات, Ordering hours, daily order limit / تعيين الحد اليومي للطلبات, Order acknowledgment, Set orders as "Completed" upon placement, Order confirmation page)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (orders/processing/..., SA-S-1736). Salla's daily order limit is not Shopify's Order limit apps (U-084, apart): what those apps limit isn't stated, and batch 1 cites them in CM-CHK-005.

capability: Order tags and automatic tagging (Salla Auto tags, order-auto-tagging)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (/orders/auto-tags, SA-S-1789). Shopify's automations that tag orders, if any, would be domain F's CM-AUT-001 (Flow); none is cited here.

capability: Deleting orders, and deleted orders kept for restoring (Salla Deleted orders, order_delete, restore-data; Shopify Orders > Delete, DELETE_ORDERS, orders/delete)
note: Salla gives deleted orders a link of its own (/orders/trash, SA-S-1892). Under CM-ORD-001 by both: Shopify's permission is Orders > Delete; Salla's link is under orders. Shopify's statements show deletion, not a store of deleted orders.

capability: Notes and comments on an order (Salla Customer notes, إضافة تعليق على الطلب, order-comment)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (orders/customer-notes, SA-S-1744). Salla's customer notes and its order comment are held together: neither is defined apart from the other, and both are notes on one order.

capability: Reorder: repeating a past order (Salla Reorder, تكرار الطلب, order-reorder)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (orders/reorder, SA-S-1746). Not domain D's CM-LOY-007, reminders to buy again, nor D's CM-B2B-005, a business buyer's saved lists. Who repeats the order, the buyer or the merchant, isn't stated.

capability: Payment methods and providers: the store's payment settings, where the merchant activates the providers and methods its buyers pay with at checkout (Shopify Payments settings, Payment providers; Salla Payments, Payment methods / طرق الدفع)
note: The root of the area's tree. Q1's M-025 joins Shopify's Payments settings page (SH-C-062) and payments apps (SH-C-076) with Salla's external gateways (SA-C-120), and its own granularity note puts Salla's Payments settings page in SA-C-110: a difference of grain, so the settings page is this parent and each kind of provider or method is a child. The later PAY batches add the children for third-party providers, wallets, instalments, manual methods and the rest.

capability: The platform's own payment service: online payments processed through the platform itself (Shopify Payments; Salla Payments / مدفوعات سلة, المدفوعات الإلكترونية)
note: Q1's M-026, joined on both platforms' definitions. Under CM-PAY-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's route payments:settings:shopify-payments sits in its payments settings (SH-S-5248), and Salla's Salla Payments is activated from its Payment methods tab (طرق الدفع, SA-S-0051) at /payments. The service's own parts (onboarding, processing behind it, payouts, fees) are its children. Its payment methods (Salla's mada, cards, Apple Pay, STC Pay; Shopify's Shop Pay and local methods) are left to the later PAY batches.

capability: Payment service onboarding and verification: the checks a store passes before it can take payments through the platform's service, its KYC and underwriting (Shopify Payments Verification and Underwriting, KYC, read_financial_kyc_information; Salla Store Verification / توثيق المتجر, /payments/kyc, kyc_new_workflow)
note: Q1's M-003. Under CM-PAY-002 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's checks are those of the Payment Services (SH-S-0132); Salla's Store Verification link is /payments/kyc (SA-S-1881) and verification opens the way to e-payments (SA-S-0137). Not domain A's CM-TRU-002, identity verification of the people behind a store, which cites Shopify's profile-assessment route and ProfileAssessment section as core under SH-C-008's keys; they are cited here only as shows. Salla's verification also serves e-commerce registration rules (domain A's CM-TRU-010).

capability: Processing, acquiring and holding funds behind the platform's payment service: the payment processors, acquirers and licensed entities that process and settle its transactions and hold the merchant's funds (Shopify Payment Processor, Financial Services Provider, Payment Facilitator, Acquirer, Regulated Payment Services; Salla عقد خدمات الدفع)
note: A grain chosen here: Shopify holds four concerns (processing and settlement, SH-C-064; custody of funds, SH-C-065; payment facilitation in the EU/EEA and UK, SH-C-066; regulated payment services in Canada, SH-C-067), all in the Shopify Payments Terms of Service and its Payment Processor List, with no admin place of their own. Q1's U-027 asks the same question of all of them against Salla's SA-C-114 and SA-C-177: who processes, holds the funds and under which licence. One capability holds them; each scope stays its statement's. Shopify gives it pages of its own: the Payment Processor List (www.shopify.com/legal/processor-list) and the regional terms.

capability: Payouts: the payment service's balance of the merchant's sales, paid out to the merchant's bank account on a schedule (Shopify Payouts, payout schedule, Shopify Payments payouts; Salla رصيد المدفوعات الإلكترونية, دورة تحويل المدفوعات الإلكترونية, list_epayments)
note: Q1's M-027. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify's payouts are Shopify Payments payouts (read_shopify_payments_payouts, View Shopify Payments payouts); Salla's e-payments balance holds what its e-payments collect (SA-S-0076). Not domain A's CM-PLN-006, Salla's prepaid store balance: Salla says the two balances differ (SA-S-0079, SA-S-0083). Not domain F's CM-PTN-003, the platform's payouts to partners. The payout bank account stays here: Shopify keeps it in SH-C-069 (read_shopify_payments_bank_accounts, bank account requirements); Salla splits it into SA-C-112.

capability: Reserves and payout holds: funds the payment service holds back from the merchant's payouts for a time (Shopify Reserves, Reserve Account, account holds)
note: Q1's M-028 (Shopify and WooCommerce). Under CM-PAY-005 by Shopify's grouping: Q1 places SH-C-070's where on its Payouts route, payments/payouts (SH-S-6325). Only Shopify shows it so far.

capability: Payment processing fees of the platform's payment service: the rates charged on the transactions it processes (Shopify Payments rates, Shopify Payments Fees, Payment rates; Salla رسوم المدفوعات الإلكترونية, حاسبة رسوم المدفوعات الإلكترونية)
note: Q1's M-029. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify's routes Shopify Payments Fees and Payment rates sit in its Payments section (SH-S-7104, SH-S-7105); Salla's fees are those of its e-payments, set by the payment services contract (SA-S-0082). Not domain A's CM-PLN-003, the platform's fee on sales through other providers (Shopify's third-party transaction fees, Salla's platform commission).

capability: Payment terms: an order paid after it is placed, on terms and a payment schedule the merchant sets (Shopify Payment terms, payment schedules, Set payment terms)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Shopify's admin grouping: its staff permissions Set payment terms sit in the categories ORDERS and DRAFT_ORDERS (SH-S-7152, SH-S-7153). Shopify's API reference lists it among its B2B resources (SH-I-0004), but no statement held limits payment terms to business buyers, so it isn't domain D's CM-B2B-001. Homonym: Salla's تعيين شروط الدفع عند الاستلام (SA-S-2027) is cash on delivery's conditions, not payment terms on an order.

capability: Chargebacks and disputes: a buyer's bank or card issuer disputes a payment, and the merchant contests it (Shopify Disputes, Chargebacks and inquiries, Manage disputes, disputes/create)
note: Q1's M-030 (WooCommerce's WC-C-116). Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify's API groups disputes in its Shopify Payments resources (SH-I-0024) with the scopes read_shopify_payments_disputes and dispute evidences, and its Shopify Payments Terms hold them in Part I, C. Contesting Chargebacks and Disputes (SH-S-0115); the admin route sits in its section Finances (risk/disputes, SH-S-7107). Not domain A's CM-TRU-020 or D's CM-SUP-008, which are buyers' complaints about a store, nor Salla's Transactions reverse (SA-C-123), a reversal the merchant makes.

capability: Chargeback protection: the platform covers the merchant against fraudulent and unrecognized chargebacks on eligible orders paid through its payment service (Shopify Protect)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify Protect "is offered as an add-on to the general Shopify Payments services" (SH-S-0402) and its route shopify-protect sits in the section Payments (SH-S-7108). Not CM-ORD-006, order risk and fraud analysis, which flags orders for the merchant to review: Shopify Protect evaluates orders too (SH-S-0404), but what it gives is cover for the chargeback. Not CM-PAY-009, the disputes themselves.

capability: Third-party payment providers and gateways: a provider other than the platform's own service that the merchant connects to take payments (Shopify Third-party payment providers, payments apps, Payments Apps API; Salla بوابات الدفع الأخرى, its external gateways)
note: The finer side of Q1's M-025: Shopify's SH-C-076 and Salla's SA-C-120 (whose batch lands it). Under CM-PAY-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's route Third-party payment providers sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7114), and Salla's other gateways are reached from its Payment methods page (SA-S-0069). Shopify's providers come as apps on its Payments Apps API; Salla's are integrations it names, each switched by a flag.

capability: Digital wallets: third-party wallets the buyer pays with (Shopify Apple Pay, Google Pay, Meta Pay, Amazon Pay; Salla المحافظ الرقمية, Apple Pay, Google Pay, stc pay)
note: Q1's U-023. Under CM-PAY-001: Shopify creates the wallets' accounts "for you to accept payments" (SH-S-0024); Salla's wallets are plan lines in its payment group (parent_code aldfaa) and PayPal is chosen from its page طرق الدفع (SA-S-0199). Salla's Apple Pay and Google Pay come through Salla Payments (SA-C-110). The wallets also give accelerated checkout buttons, which CM-CHK-008 holds (SH-S-0419).

capability: PayPal as a payment method (Shopify PayPal Express Checkout, PayPal Wallet; Salla PayPal الدفع عبر)
note: Q1's M-032. Under CM-PAY-012 by the grouping both platforms share: Shopify's plan row is PayPal Wallet rates (SH-S-7024), and Salla says PayPal is available as a digital wallet option (يتوفر PayPal كخيار للمحفظة الرقمية, SA-S-0199). Q1's granularity note: Salla's concern also holds stc pay direct and Mokafaa Al Rajhi, which aren't PayPal. Batch 7 lands Salla's SA-C-119 in the parent CM-PAY-012, as coarser than PayPal (the coordinator).

capability: Saved buyer checkout details: the platform saves the buyer's payment method and address so that checkout goes faster (Shop Pay; Salla حفظ بطاقة وعنوان العميل)
note: Q1's U-026. Under CM-CHK-008 by Shopify's grouping: its Shop Pay Merchant Terms put Shop Pay under "1. Accelerated Checkout (Shop Pay)" (SH-S-0413), and Shopify says accelerated checkouts "save customer payment and shipping information" (SH-S-7287, cited in CM-CHK-008). Shopify's admin route for it sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7111), and Shop Pay "only enables payment processing through the sharing of payment credentials" (SH-S-0408), so the area is PAY. Salla's side is a join on role, a reading: its shopping experience fee includes the services of saving the customer's card and address (SA-S-0104). Whether Salla's saved details serve the buyer in other stores isn't stated.

capability: Instalments and buy now, pay later: the buyer pays for an order later or in instalments (Shopify Shop Pay Installments; Salla وسائل الدفع الآجلة, الدفع بالتقسيط عبر تابي وتمارا)
note: Q1's M-031. Under CM-PAY-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's route shop-pay-installments sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7112); Salla's deferred payment methods are a section of its payment methods page (SA-S-0070). Shopify's is offered under a Merchant Agreement with Affirm (SH-S-0126); Salla's are providers it names (Tabby, Tamara and others). Homonym: Salla's الدفع الآجل here is buy now pay later, not CM-PAY-008's payment terms.

capability: Manual payment methods: methods paid outside the online payment flow, such as cash on delivery and bank transfer (Shopify Manual payment methods, Record payments, Mark as paid; Salla الدفع عند الاستلام / Cash on delivery, التحويل البنكي)
note: Q1's M-033, a difference of grain: Shopify keeps these methods in one concern (SH-C-079), while Salla splits cash on delivery by who collects it (SA-C-115 through Salla's shipping labels, SA-C-116 through the merchant's own carrier) and keeps bank transfer apart (SA-C-117). The Salla batches may add children for them. Joined by definition: Shopify names "manual payment methods such as cash, cash on delivery (COD), and bank transfers" (SH-S-0322). Under CM-PAY-001: Shopify's route Manual payment methods sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7117); Salla's cash on delivery setting sits under shipping (shipping/shipping.cod, SA-S-1765) and its bank accounts under its payment methods (SA-S-0095). Batch 7 adds its children CM-PAY-029, cash on delivery, and CM-PAY-030, bank transfer (the coordinator).

capability: Local payment methods: region-specific ways to pay, offered through the platform's payment service (Shopify Local payment methods, Accept local payment methods*, managed payment methods; Salla KNET through مدفوعات سلة for Kuwait stores)
note: Q1's U-024. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify's are activated "with Shopify Payments" (SH-S-0420) under its route shopify-payments:local-payment-methods; Salla's KNET "is available through Salla Payments for Kuwait stores" (SA-S-0065). Salla's side is a join on role, a reading: Salla doesn't call KNET local; its statement scopes it to Kuwait's stores. Salla's KNET through Tap (SA-S-0130) is a gateway, in CM-PAY-011.

capability: Cryptocurrency and stablecoin payments (Shopify cryptocurrency gateways, USDC rates, Cryptocurrency Payment Protocol)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far, and Q1's U-025 holds only WooCommerce on the other side. Under CM-PAY-001: Shopify places it on its Payments settings (settings/payments, SH-S-6328), through third-party cryptocurrency gateways (SH-S-0428) and through Shopify Payments in eligible regions (SH-S-0433). Shopify's Cryptocurrency Credit Reward Program pays some credits in stablecoins (SH-S-0434); that is shows here.

capability: Payment method rules: conditions that hide, reorder or restrict the payment methods a buyer is offered at checkout (Shopify Payment customizations, the Payment Customization function; Salla Payment restrictions / قيود الدفع)
note: Q1's U-022, a join on role, a reading: Shopify's function can "rename, reorder, hide the payment methods available to customers during checkout" (SH-S-0589); Salla's payment restrictions are "conditions imposed on payment options", such as restricting a payment method for some countries or customers (SA-S-5050). Under CM-PAY-001 by the grouping both share: Shopify's route Payment customizations sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7119), Salla's link Payment restrictions at /payments/rules (SA-S-1877). Salla gives fraud as the reason; Shopify's statements give none (Q1 gap). Shopify lists it among its Function APIs as well; batch 1's function capabilities (CM-CHK-005, -006) have no parent, but this one's admin route and Salla's both sit in payments.

capability: Payment transactions on an order: authorizing, capturing and recording an order's payments, and acting on a transaction afterwards (Shopify order transactions, Payment authorization and capture, Capture payments; Salla Transactions / عمليات الدفع الإلكتروني)
note: Q1's M-034, one-to-one by the term transactions: Shopify's concern covers authorization and capture (SH-C-084), Salla's the refund, void and reverse of a transaction (SA-C-123). Both give it a place of its own: Shopify's webhook topics order_transactions/create and tender_transactions/create and its staff permission Orders > Capture payments; Salla's link Transactions at /payments/transactions (SA-S-1880), its API folder Transactions and its scope transactions. Parent CM-ORD-001 by Shopify's admin grouping: its where is the Orders page (SH-S-6322) and its permissions sit under Orders and Drafts. Salla's grouping differs: its link sits in the payments list (/payments/transactions) and its permission payments_operations_management in the group إعدادات المتجر, while its refund permission order_refund_payment sits in the group الطلبات (see notes). The refund itself is RET's: Salla's refund permission is shows here.

capability: In-person card payments: card payments the buyer makes at the point of sale, processed through the platform's payment service or a provider (Shopify In-person card rates, Shopify Payments for POS, card_present_payments, Tap to Pay; Salla الدفع بالبطاقة في كاشير سلة بوينت, SoftPOS)
note: The payment's processing, its rates and its rules, not the point of sale or its devices: domain E holds the point of sale (CM-POS-001) and its card-present devices (CM-POS-002), whose note leaves the card payment's processing and rates to domain C (SH-C-086). Shopify gives it a place of its own: the plan rows In-person card rates and In-person manual rates (SH-S-7027, SH-S-7029) and the billing category Tap to Pay transaction fees (SH-I-1352). Q1's M-036 joins SH-C-086 with WooCommerce's WC-C-014; no Salla concern of domain C holds it, and Salla's side is SA-C-095's (domain E, which names C under also for its Geidea card-present payment statements). Under CM-PAY-001, the grouping the two share, a reading: Shopify's in-person payments run through Shopify Payments (SH-S-0436, SH-S-0047), Salla's through Geidea (SA-S-5040), so CM-PAY-002, the platform's own service, would fit Shopify's side only.

capability: Saved customer payment methods and payment mandates: payment methods the store keeps for a customer and charges for later orders without the customer going through checkout (Shopify customer payment methods, payment mandates, Charge vaulted payment method)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far; Q1's M-035 holds it with WooCommerce's payment tokens (WC-C-098, WC-C-042). Its own place: the customer's route Payment methods (SH-S-7120), the scopes read_customer_payment_methods, read_payment_mandate and write_payment_mandate, the webhook topics customer_payment_methods/create, /update and /revoke and the staff permissions Orders > Charge vaulted payment method and PAY_ORDERS_BY_VAULTED_CARD. Not CM-PAY-014, saved buyer checkout details, a reading: Shop Pay saves the buyer's details "making the checkout process faster" (SH-S-0406), while these are stored to pay for future orders "without requiring the customer to manually go through checkout" (SH-S-0592), charged by the store. No parent: Shopify's route sits on the customer's record (section Customers, domain D's) and its permissions under Orders and Drafts; neither is a capability of this area. Salla's flag checkout-save-cards (SA-S-3123, SA-C-110) saves cards at checkout and is left to the Salla batches for CM-PAY-014 (notes).

capability: The merchant's money account with the platform: a business account in the admin that receives the store's sales and holds and spends the merchant's money (Shopify Balance, Banking)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Its own place: the admin section Banking (SH-S-1547), the routes shopify-balance/* and access_account/shopify-balance, the plan row Manage money with Shopify Balance (SH-S-7062) and the staff permission View Balance account activity (SH-S-7168). Not A's CM-PLN-006, Salla's prepaid store balance with the platform, spent on the platform's services, nor D's CM-LOY-001, the buyer's wallet with the store, nor CM-PAY-005, the payment service's payouts, which may be paid into it (SH-S-0347). No parent: Shopify's own grouping puts it in its Finance suite (SH-S-0454) beside Shopify Credit and Shopify Capital (CM-PAY-025, CM-PAY-026), not in Settings > Payments; no capability holds the Finance suite as such (notes). Parent of CM-PAY-024.

capability: Business cards on the merchant's money account: payment cards the merchant spends its account's money with (Shopify Balance Visa® Commercial cards, Cards)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Its own place: the admin route finance/cards (SH-S-5098) and the section Cards (SH-S-1552). Under CM-PAY-023 by Shopify's own name, Shopify Balance Visa® Commercial cards, and its rule that personal use of the card may end the Shopify Balance account (SH-S-0465). Q1 split it from the account because the card's issuer (Celtic Bank) differs from the account's funds holder. The route's unlock also takes the permission MANAGE_ALL_SHOPIFY_CREDIT_CARDS (SH-S-5099), Shopify Credit's (CM-PAY-025).

capability: Business credit for the merchant: a charge card with a credit limit, issued to the merchant and paid in full or repaid from its sales (Shopify Credit, Shopify Credit pay-in-full Visa® card)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Its own place: the admin section Credit (SH-S-1559), the routes credit and access_account/credit, the plan row Shopify Credit pay-in-full Visa® card (SH-S-7064) and the staff permission View all Shopify Credit account activity (SH-S-7169). Not CM-PAY-026: Shopify Credit is a card account with a credit limit set by the issuing bank (SH-S-7267), while Capital is funding repaid from a share of sales. Shopify Credit's Program Terms are an agreement with Shopify Capital Inc. (SH-S-7276), a company of Shopify's group by its name; whether that company offers Capital isn't stated in the statements held. Not CM-PAY-024: Credit has its own section and route, apart from Cards. No parent, as for CM-PAY-023.

capability: Merchant financing repaid from sales: funding the platform offers or arranges for the merchant, as a loan or a merchant cash advance, repaid from a share of the store's sales (Shopify Capital; Salla capital / financial-support, صندوق سلة)
note: Q1's M-038, a difference of grain: Shopify splits Shopify Capital by country, because the lender differs (SH-C-091 to SH-C-097), Salla keeps one concern (SA-C-128). One capability holds all seven Shopify concerns, each statement keeping its country scope: they share one admin section Capital (SH-S-1551), one route access_account/capital, one entitlement shopifyFinance.capital and one plan row, and differ only by lender and agreement, which are slot fillers. Both define it as financing repaid from sales: Shopify's loan repayments "from a daily percentage rate of your daily sales" (SH-S-0482), Salla's collection of 25% of net sales from each payment (SA-S-0111). Both give it a place: Shopify's section Capital and plan row Flexible growth funding through Shopify Capital (SH-S-7063); Salla's flag financial-support, released on the Pro and Special plans (SA-S-3487), and its dashboard's capital.* texts. No parent, as for CM-PAY-023.

capability: Paying the merchant's bills to its vendors: the merchant schedules and pays its business bills from the platform (Shopify Bill Pay)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Its own place: the admin routes finance:billpay and finance:billpay:redirect, gated by the feature canAccessBillPay and the entitlement shopifyFinance.billPay (SH-S-5166, SH-S-5167), and the plan row Schedule, pay, and manage bills with Shopify Bill Pay (SH-S-7065). Bills are paid "using a bank account or your Shopify Balance account" (SH-S-0501), so it is not a child of CM-PAY-023: the money account is one source of payment among others. No parent, as for CM-PAY-023, -025 and -026, the other parts of Shopify's Finance pages. Not A's CM-PLN-005 (paying the platform's bills) nor CM-PLN-004: these are the merchant's own bills to its vendors. "Bills" is a homonym (notes, batch 6).

capability: Accounting and ERP integrations: connecting the store's sales and finances to an accounting system or an ERP (Shopify Accounting apps, ERP apps; Salla Accounting & Finance / المحاسبة والمالية, ERP system, الربط مع الخدمات المحاسبية)
note: Q1's M-077, one-to-one. Both give it a place of its own as an app category: Shopify's App Store categories Accounting apps and ERP apps (SH-S-2706, SH-S-2613), Salla's app categories Accounting & Finance and ERP system (SA-S-1194, SA-S-1195, SA-S-1222). Salla also gives it plan lines (الربط مع الخدمات المحاسبية, سلة برو) and released flags for named accounting services. Area PAY by the seed's "balance and finances"; scope.tsv names G under also for both concerns. No parent: neither platform groups it under its payment settings.

capability: Cash on delivery: the buyer pays in cash when the order is delivered, and the amount reaches the merchant through the platform or directly from the carrier (Salla الدفع عند الاستلام / Cash on delivery, through بوليصات سلة or the merchant's own carrier; Shopify cash on delivery (COD), a manual payment method)
note: Q1's M-033, a difference of grain: Salla gives cash on delivery a place of its own, its setting Cash on delivery (shipping/shipping.cod, SA-S-1765) and its plan lines الدفع عند الاستلام and تعيين شروط الدفع عند الاستلام, and splits it by who collects (SA-C-115 through Salla's shipping labels, SA-C-116 through the merchant's own carrier). One capability holds both: the split is who collects and settles, which the cells' placements show (core where Salla transfers the balance from its labels' carriers, SA-S-0122; outside where the carrier settles with the merchant, SA-S-0120, SA-S-0121). Under CM-PAY-016 by Shopify's grouping, which names cash on delivery among its manual payment methods (SH-S-0322); Salla's setting sits under shipping. Homonym: Salla's cash-on-delivery balance in its wallet (SA-S-0106) is not the e-payments balance of CM-PAY-005.

capability: Bank transfer as a payment method: the buyer pays by transfer to a bank account the store shows at checkout (Salla التحويل البنكي, bank_accounts_management / إدارة الحسابات البنكية, نظام المدفوعات الفورية عبر سريع; Shopify bank transfers, a manual payment method)
note: Q1's M-033, a difference of grain: Salla keeps bank transfer apart (SA-C-117) and gives it plan lines and a staff permission of its own (SA-S-1956, SA-S-1957, SA-S-2435). Under CM-PAY-016 by Shopify's grouping (SH-S-0322). Homonym: this bank account, shown to customers at checkout (SA-S-0095), is not the payout account of CM-PAY-005 (SA-C-112), which Salla's help says isn't shown to them.

capability: Amounts withheld from the merchant's wallet for app partners: an app the merchant installs has the platform hold an amount of the merchant's balance and settle it with the partner (Salla Settlements / إدارة المبالغ المحجوزة, Create Instant Settlement, managed settlement)
note: Salla gives it a place of its own: the Merchant API folder Settlements and the access scope settlements (إدارة المبالغ المحجوزة), whose instant-settlement endpoint is allowed only for dropshipping applications (SA-S-0179). Salla's shipping apps' managed settlement (SA-C-145, SA-S-5065, SA-S-5066) withholds label amounts from the wallet the same way, a reading. Homonym: this settlement, between the merchant and an app partner, is not the payment processors' settlement of transactions (CM-PAY-004). Kept apart from B's CM-CAT-010 (sourcing by dropshipping apps, which cites SA-C-124's category and endpoint as extension-point), F's CM-APP-003 (the platform billing the merchant for an app) and A's CM-PLN-006 (the store balance itself). No parent: the wallet it withholds from is domain A's.

capability: Payment links: a link to pay for an order that the merchant sends the buyer (Salla إرسال رابط الدفع للعميل)
note: Salla gives it a plan line of its own (SA-S-1968, in its payment group) and sends the link from the order's actions (SA-S-5143); under CM-ORD-001 by that admin place, a reading. Shopify's draft orders' invoices (SH-S-7225, CM-ORD-008) aren't stated to carry a link to pay (U-018, apart).

capability: Taxes on the store's sales: the store's tax settings, the taxes and rates it charges its buyers and how its prices show them (Shopify Taxes and duties, MANAGE_TAXES_SETTINGS, read_taxes; Salla Taxes / الضرائب, Tax settings / إعدادات الضريبة, tax_management, taxes, ضريبة القيمة المضافة)
note: Q1's M-040 (SH-C-100, SA-C-160). Both give it a place of its own: Shopify's settings section Taxes and duties at /settings/taxes (SH-S-1492, SH-S-7123), its staff permission and its scopes read_taxes and write_taxes; Salla's settings link Taxes at /taxes-and-duties (SA-S-1686), its Tax settings at /payments/taxes (SA-S-1879), its Merchant API folder Taxes, its scope taxes and its staff permission tax_management. It is the parent of the TAX area: Shopify puts registrations, VAT validation, tax providers and duties under the same Taxes section (paths add, ioss, vat-number-validation, providers, duties: SH-S-7124 to SH-S-7129), and Salla's one link is Taxes and duties. Not A's CM-PLN-007, the taxes on the platform's own charges to the merchant: there Shopify's "Tax registration" is the merchant's tax ID for Shopify's bills (SH-S-0279), a homonym of the store's registrations to collect tax (CM-TAX-003).

capability: The platform's automated tax calculation service: the platform works out the sales tax and VAT on the store's orders and keeps the rates current (Shopify Tax, Automated sales tax calculations, shopifyTax)
note: Shopify gives it a place of its own: the plan line Automated sales tax calculations (SH-S-7066), the store entitlement shopifyTax, the built-in features pages Shopify Tax (EU, UK, US) and its own terms (www.shopify.com/legal/shopify-tax-terms). Under CM-TAX-001 by Shopify's grouping: the Taxes settings route is gated by the entitlement shopifyTax.enabled (SH-S-5271), and SH-C-100 holds both the default rates and Shopify Tax. WooCommerce's split (WC-C-054, merchant-entered rates; WC-C-055, WooCommerce Tax) is the same cut (M-040's granularity).

capability: Tax registrations: the store's registrations with the tax authorities where it must collect tax, the tax number it records and shows, and tracking where it is liable (Shopify Tax registrations, add-registration, IOSS registration, Tax liability tracking; Salla الرقم الضريبي, التسجيل في هيئة الزكاة والضريبة والجمارك)
note: Shopify gives it a place of its own: the Taxes section's routes add (add-registration) and ioss (SH-S-7124, SH-S-7125) and the plan line Tax liability tracking (SH-S-7067). Q1 split SH-C-101 from calculation "because the merchant decides where it is registered while Shopify computes". Under CM-TAX-001 by Shopify's paths in its Taxes section. Homonym: Shopify's "Tax registration" for Shopify's own bills (SH-S-0279) is A's CM-PLN-007.

capability: Third-party tax services: tax apps and providers that calculate the store's taxes in place of the platform's own (Shopify Tax apps, tax_calculation, Manage tax provider, tax_services/create, write_taxes, Advanced tax platform; Salla avalara-tax)
note: Shopify gives it a place of its own: the App Store category Tax apps (SH-S-2708), the extension point tax_calculation (SH-S-2256), the Taxes section's route providers, "Manage tax provider" (SH-S-7127), and the plan line Advanced tax platform (SH-S-7069). Under CM-TAX-001 by Shopify's own route (Taxes > providers) and because a tax app "replaces Shopify's tax service for that store" (SH-S-0530).

capability: VAT number validation, tax exemptions and VAT invoices: business buyers enter a VAT number that is validated to claim the reverse charge exemption, buyers are exempted from tax, and the VAT invoices that follow (Shopify VAT validation, exemptions, and invoicing; VAT validation in checkout)
note: Shopify gives it a place of its own: the plan line "VAT validation, exemptions, and invoicing" (SH-S-7068) and the Taxes section's route vat-number-validation (SH-S-7126). One capability at Shopify's grain: its plan line holds the three together, and its help centre puts VAT validation and VAT invoices under "Shopify Tax features for the European Union and United Kingdom" (SH-I-2330). Under CM-TAX-001 by Shopify's route. Not C's CM-ORD-008: that is the order's invoice as the store issues and prints it; what is here is the VAT treatment Shopify Tax applies.

capability: Automated tax filing: the store's sales tax returns prepared, filed and remitted through the platform (Shopify Tax Automated Filing, Automated filing, taxes/filing, taxFilingEnabled)
note: Shopify gives it a place of its own: the admin route taxes/filing (SH-S-5269), the billing charge category Automated filing (SH-I-1324), its own terms (Shopify Tax Automated Filing Terms of Service, SH-S-0040). Under CM-TAX-002 by Shopify's grouping: "Automated filing with Shopify Tax", available only for stores in the United States that use Shopify Tax (SH-S-0522). Closed to new enrollment and ending for sales after December 31, 2026 (SH-S-0521, SH-S-0525). Not the same thing as Salla's e-invoicing with ZATCA (CM-TAX-007): a return is filed for a period's sales; an e-invoice is reported invoice by invoice (U-031, apart).

capability: E-invoicing with the tax authority: the store's tax invoices linked and uploaded electronically to the tax authority through the platform (Salla الربط مع هيئة الزكاة والضريبة, الربط بهيئة الزكاة والضريبة والجمارك, zatca)
note: Salla gives it a place of its own: an app installed from its app store, الربط مع هيئة الزكاة والضريبة (SA-S-0151), the released flag zatca of type app (SA-S-3219) and the plan line الربط بهيئة الزكاة والضريبة والجمارك (SA-S-2120, سلة برو). For stores in Saudi Arabia only (SA-S-0149). Q1 split SA-C-161 from Salla's taxes per market and from order invoices (SA-C-044, C's CM-ORD-008). No parent: no statement held puts it under Salla's tax settings or its invoice settings (the plan line's parent_code mhfth-almtgr-oalfotr has no title held). Not Shopify's automated filing (CM-TAX-006) nor its VAT invoices (CM-TAX-005): U-031, apart.

capability: Duties and import taxes on cross-border orders: estimating, collecting and settling the customs duties and import taxes on what the store ships abroad (Shopify Duties and import taxes, Estimate and collect duties and taxes, Duty; Salla الرسوم الجمركية, إظهار حقل المعلومات الجمركية)
note: Q1's M-042 (SH-C-105, SA-C-162). Shopify gives it a place of its own: the Taxes section's route duties (SH-S-7129), the plan line Estimate and collect duties and taxes (SH-S-7079), the Admin API object Duty (SH-S-7456) and its billing charge categories. Under CM-TAX-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's Taxes and duties settings, Salla's link Taxes at /taxes-and-duties. A merchant of record that handles duties for the store, such as Shopify's Managed Markets, is E's CM-MKS-003; product customs data for shipping (Salla SA-C-146, HS codes) is the SHP batch's.

capability: Tax forms the platform issues to the merchant: the tax documents the platform files with the tax authority about the merchant's receipts and gives the merchant (Shopify 1099-K and 1099-MISC tax forms, VIEW_TAX_DOCUMENTS)
note: Shopify gives it a place of its own: the admin routes finance/tax-forms/1099-k and finance/tax-forms/1099-misc (SH-S-7121, SH-S-7122) and the staff permission VIEW_TAX_DOCUMENTS. The forms report the merchant's receipts: the 1099-K "is generated by Shopify Payments and is provided to you and to the IRS annually" (SH-S-0505). Not A's CM-PLN-007 (taxes on Shopify's charges) nor CM-PAY-002: the payment service is the filer, the forms are a tax document. The routes are in the admin section Banking (C's CM-PAY-023), but no statement puts the forms under it, so no parent. Scope: United States.

capability: Shipping and delivery: the store's shipping setup, the zones it ships to and the rates its buyers pay, set in the platform's shipping settings (Shopify Shipping and delivery, shipping profiles, Shipping and fulfillment, read_shipping; Salla Shipping & delivery, Shipping settings, Shipping Zones, shippings, تخصيص تسعيرة الشحن)
note: Q1's M-045 (SH-C-114, SA-C-142, WC-C-075). The area's parent: both platforms put the area's other subjects under it. Shopify's routes for carrier services, order routing, local delivery and pickup in store are paths of its section Shipping (SH-S-7133, SH-S-7140, SH-S-7136, SH-S-7137), and its store entitlement shipping holds both settingsAccess and labels (SH-S-5842). Salla's plan lines for its own labels, branch pickup and rates share the parent_code alshhn-oaltosyl (SA-S-2018, SA-S-2029, SA-S-2023), and its Shipment log sits in the same admin list (list 8) as Shipping & delivery and Shipping settings (SA-S-1871, SA-S-1868). Both API groupings put fulfilment with shipping: Shopify's resource group Shipping and fulfillment (SH-S-0786), Salla's developer section Shipments & Fulfillment APIs (SA-S-1171). Salla's shipping restrictions (قيود الشحن والتوصيل; shipping_rules_management, قيود شركات الشحن; restrict-shipping-companies-by-country) are cited here: no statement held defines them, so they are not joined with Shopify's delivery customization (CM-SHP-013). Homonym: Shopify's route shipping-calculator (SH-S-5262, here) and Salla's plan line حاسبة تكلفة الشحن (SA-S-2024, CM-SHP-002), each undefined. Customer addresses are D's CM-CUS-008.

capability: Shipping labels bought through the platform: the merchant buys and prints carriers' shipping labels in the admin, at the platform's rates, and pays for them through its account with the platform (Shopify Shipping, Shipping labels, Buy and print shipping labels; Salla بوليصات سلة, بوليصات شحن سلة المُخفضة, Shipping label cost deduction)
note: Q1's M-047 (SH-C-116, SA-C-140, WC-C-060): "Each is the platform's own label-buying service with integrated carriers." Under CM-SHP-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's entitlement shipping holds labels beside settingsAccess (SH-S-5842); Salla's plan line sits under alshhn-oaltosyl (SA-S-2018). Both say the carrier, not the platform, carries: Shopify "serves only as an intermediary" between the merchant and the Third-Party Integrator or Third-Party Shipping Provider (SH-S-0613); Salla's labels follow the approved carriers' cancellation and return policies (SA-S-5060). Homonym: بوليصة (policy) is Salla's word for a shipping label, an air waybill (AWB), not a store policy (E's CM-CNT-008). The merchant's own carrier account used with the platform's labels (Shopify SH-S-0616) is cited here; Salla's own-contract carriers (SA-C-141) are batch 11's. Customs fees on Salla's labels (SA-S-5075) are core in CM-TAX-008, shows here.

capability: Shipping insurance: insurance on a shipment sent with the platform's shipping labels (Shopify Shipping insurance, Third-Party Shipping Insurance)
note: Shopify gives it a plan line, Shipping insurance*, included on every plan (SH-S-7047), and a billing charge category Insurance premiums (SH-I-1331). Under CM-SHP-002 by Shopify's own words: "If you ship orders from the United States and you buy shipping labels, then you can protect your orders by purchasing shipping insurance" (SH-S-0720), and "Labels from Shopify include ... up to $200 insurance" (SH-S-7220). Homonym: تأمين in Salla's packaging statement (SA-S-5069) is securing packaging, not insurance.

capability: Third-party calculated shipping rates: shipping rates shown to the buyer that a carrier or an app's carrier service calculates, in place of the merchant's own rates (Shopify 3rd-party calculated shipping rates, CarrierService, DeliveryCarrierService, Shipping rate apps, Manage preferred carriers)
note: Shopify gives it a plan line (SH-S-7048: not included on Basic, an add-on on Grow, included on Advanced and Plus), a route in its section Shipping (carrier-services/:id, Manage preferred carriers, SH-S-7133), the API resource CarrierService and an App Store category Shipping rate apps (SH-S-2629); hence under CM-SHP-001. No statement held says how the rates are calculated beyond the plan line's name. Q1's U-072 sets SH-C-115 among Salla's carriers and shipping apps (SA-C-139, SA-C-141, SA-C-145), which land in batch 11.

capability: Order routing: rules that assign an order to the locations that fulfil it (Shopify Order routing, Order Routing Location Rule, fulfillment_orders/order_routing_complete)
note: You can set up order routing to automatically assign orders to fulfillment locations based on configured rules (SH-S-0751). Under CM-SHP-001 by Shopify's route order_routing in its section Shipping (SH-S-7140). Apps write rules through the Function API Order Routing Location Rule. Not B's CM-INV-009 (inventory withdrawal priority), whose Shopify cell is none-held and whose Salla cell holds Branch and warehouse priority order (SA-S-1755); not C's CM-ORD-007 (assignment to staff); not G's CM-OPS-001, which cites Salla's automatic assignment of an order to the next carrier by priority (SA-S-0162). Locations are B's CM-INV-005. Salla's Shipping Routes (SA-C-143, U-020) are batch 11's: no statement held defines them.

capability: Local pickup and local delivery: getting an order to a buyer near the store's own locations, by the buyer's pickup or the store's own delivery (Shopify Local pickup, Local delivery; Salla الاستلام من الفرع, Branch Delivery Zones)
note: Q1's M-046 (SH-C-121, SA-C-148): each platform's concern holds both. A parent at their grain, with a child for each (CM-SHP-007, CM-SHP-008), since Shopify gives each a route of its own (SH-S-7137, SH-S-7136) and Salla gives pickup a plan line and local delivery an API folder. Under CM-SHP-001: Shopify's routes are in its section Shipping; Salla's pickup plan line is under alshhn-oaltosyl (SA-S-2029). Homonym: الفرع in Salla's economy shipping "(استلام وتسليم من الفرع)" (SA-S-2020, CM-SHP-002) is a carrier's branch, not the store's; Shopify's pickup points (SH-C-124, batch 11) are a carrier's too.

capability: Local pickup: the buyer collects the order at one of the store's locations (Shopify Pickup in store, Local pick up, product pickup locations; Salla إتاحة الاستلام من الفرع)
note: Shopify's route pickup_in_store (SH-S-7137), its webhook topic fulfillment_orders/line_items_prepared_for_pickup and the Storefront scope unauthenticated_read_product_pickup_locations; Salla's plan line إتاحة الاستلام من الفرع (Salla Plus, SA-S-2029). Neither platform defines it beyond its name in what is held.

capability: Local delivery: the store's own delivery of orders to buyers near its locations (Shopify Local delivery; Salla Branch Delivery Zones)
note: Shopify's route local_deliveries (SH-S-7136) and its webhook topic fulfillment_orders/line_items_prepared_for_local_delivery; Salla's Merchant API folder Branch Delivery Zones (SA-S-1071). Neither defines it beyond its name in what is held: that Salla's branch delivery zones are the store's own delivery, as Shopify's local delivery is, is Q1's match M-046, a reading.

capability: Order fulfilment: sending an order's items to the buyer, recorded on the order as fulfillments or shipments (Shopify Fulfillment orders, fulfillments, Fulfill and ship, FulfillmentOrder; Salla Shipments, Shipment log, order.shipment.created)
note: Q1's M-048 (SH-C-118, WC-C-092); U-073 sets SH-C-118 and SH-C-126 against Salla's Shipments (SA-C-144) and shipping apps (SA-C-145), which land in batch 11. Salla's cell is a join on role (a reading): Shopify's permission names the act Fulfill and ship (SH-S-6169, the user's fulfill_and_ship_orders), and Salla's shipments are created and cancelled for an order (order.shipment.created, order.shipment.cancelled) and first updated by the carrier (SA-S-1637). Under CM-SHP-001 by the grouping both share: Shopify's API group Shipping and fulfillment (SH-S-0786) and Salla's Shipment log in its shipping list (SA-S-1871); Shopify's staff permission also puts it under Orders. C's CM-ORD-009 (packing slips) may belong under it (notes).

capability: Fulfillment batching: the admin section Batches, open to stores eligible for fulfillment batching (Shopify Batches, fulfillmentBatchingEligible)
note: Shopify gives it an admin section of its own (section Batches, path batches, SH-S-7134), gated by the permission ORDERS and the store feature fulfillmentBatchingEligible (SH-S-7135), false in the captured trial stores and true in the development stores (SH-S-5792, SH-S-5794); hence under CM-SHP-009 by the feature's name. No statement held says what a batch holds. Salla's plan line إدارة مجموعة طلبات كدفعة واحدة (managing a group of orders as one batch, SA-S-1996) is C's CM-ORD-001: nothing held ties it to fulfilment.

capability: Fulfillment services and third-party logistics: an app or provider that stores the merchant's stock and prepares and ships its orders, taking the orders to fulfil from the platform (Shopify Fulfillment services, FulfillmentService, Third-party logistics (3PL) apps; Salla Fulfillment apps)
note: Shopify: "Fulfillment service apps provide third-party warehousing, print on demand, or fulfillment services that prepare and ship orders on behalf of merchants" (SH-S-0702); they "can accept or reject requests to fulfill orders" (SH-S-0704), on the fulfillment orders their scopes reach (SH-S-5934), hence under CM-SHP-009. Its App Store category Third-party logistics (3PL) apps (SH-S-2631) and billing category External 3PL transaction fees (SH-I-1329). Salla's app category Fulfillment (SA-S-1192) is read as the same role (a reading), with its unreleased flag shipping-fulfillment-centers. A fulfillment service's location is B's CM-INV-005 (SH-S-0703); dropshipping and print on demand as sourcing are B's CM-CAT-010.

capability: Fulfillment network offered in the platform's admin: one service that connects the merchant with logistics providers that store its stock and fulfil its orders (Shopify Fulfillment Network, Shopify Logistics)
note: You can use the Fulfillment Network to connect with third-party logistics providers (3PLs) that store your inventory and fulfill orders on your behalf (SH-S-0715), hence under CM-SHP-011. Shopify gives it an admin section (ShopifyFulfillmentNetwork, SH-S-1603), its own terms of service (SH-I-1390) and billing charge categories (SH-I-1347 to SH-I-1349, Shopify Logistics among them). It is installed from the Shopify App Store (SH-S-0716), and its route is gated by the apps permission (SH-S-5095). No statement held names Shopify's company as its maker (a gap), so the cell is not own-service.

capability: Delivery customization: app-written rules that change the delivery options a buyer is offered at checkout (Shopify Delivery Customization, a Shopify Function API, read_delivery_customizations)
note: Shopify's Function API Delivery Customization (SH-S-0855, target delivery_customization) with its scopes, and its help-centre section Customizing payment methods and delivery options at checkout (SH-I-2119). No parent, as batch 1's function capabilities (CM-CHK-005, -006): Shopify lists it among its Function APIs, and no admin route of it is held. No statement held says what a rule can do to an option. Salla's shipping restrictions (قيود الشحن والتوصيل) are in CM-SHP-001: with neither side defined, a join on role would rest on names only. F's CM-APP-005 holds functions as such; payment methods' counterpart is CM-PAY-019.

capability: Fulfillment constraints: rules an app's function sets on how orders are fulfilled (Shopify Fulfillment Constraints, a Shopify Function API, read_fulfillment_constraint_rules)
note: Shopify's Function API Fulfillment Constraints (SH-S-0857, target fulfillment_constraints), its scopes and the mutation fulfillmentConstraintRuleCreate, which the app that deployed the function invokes to register the rule (SH-S-6204). No statement held says what a constraint does: the name is Shopify's. No parent, as CM-SHP-013.

capability: Shipping carriers: the shipping companies a store ships with, connected in the platform's admin, whether under the platform's contracts or the merchant's own carrier account or contract (Salla Shipping Companies, شركات الشحن, ربط خاص بـ 190+ شركة شحن, ربط عقد ... الخاص بك, shipping.company.created; Shopify supported carriers, own Third-Party Shipping Provider account, Tracking carriers)
note: Salla gives it places of its own: its Merchant API folder Shipping Companies (SA-S-1045) with the topics shipping.company.created, .updated and .deleted, the plan lines ربط خاص بـ 190+ شركة شحن and شحن محلي وعالمي مع أكثر من 100 شركة شحن, its app type Shipping App "for shipping companies" (SA-S-1185) and one released feature flag per integrated carrier. Q1 split SA-C-139 (carriers named in flags and plan lines, "a flag or plan line naming a carrier does not say under whose contract the carrier" works) from SA-C-141 (the merchant's own carriers and contracts); both land here, the contract being a grain inside one capability, since no place of its own is held for either side of the split (notes, batch 11). Under CM-SHP-001 by both platforms' grouping: Salla's carriers are in its Shipping & delivery section and its plan lines share the parent_code alshhn-oaltosyl; Shopify's carrier account is connected "with Shopify Shipping" (SH-S-0616). The labels bought at the platform's rates through these carriers are CM-SHP-002. Homonym: Salla's flag track (SA-S-3081) is a carrier's name among the carriers' flags, not tracking (CM-SHP-017).

capability: Shipping routes: the section Shipping Routes of the platform's shipping settings (Salla Shipping Routes, shipping-routes)
note: Salla gives it a place of its own: the admin link Shipping Routes at /shipping/setting/routes (SA-S-1872), a Merchant API folder Shipping Routes beside Shipping Zones and Shipping Companies (SA-S-1047) and another in its shipping apps' APIs (SA-S-1118), and the released flag shipping-routes (plans pro and special). No statement held says what a route is: Q1's unclear candidate U-020 reads them as "routing to carriers", a reading not stated. Not Shopify's order routing (CM-SHP-005), which assigns orders to fulfillment locations (U-020, apart). Under CM-SHP-001 by its path in Salla's shipping settings.

capability: Shipment tracking: the tracking of an order's shipment, its tracking information and the carriers it can name, shown to the merchant and the buyer (Shopify Order tracking, FulfillmentTrackingInfo, Tracking carriers, Order tracking apps; Salla تتبع الطلب عبر محفظة أبل (Apple Wallet))
note: Shopify gives it places of its own: the App Store category Order tracking apps (SH-S-2620), its built-in feature Order tracking, at the customer notifications settings with surface_detail=order-tracking (SH-S-7208), and the Admin API object FulfillmentTrackingInfo; Salla a plan line, تتبع الطلب عبر محفظة أبل (Apple Wallet), Salla Plus (SA-S-1995, SA-C-040's, left here by batch 2). Under CM-SHP-009 by Shopify's object, "the tracking information for a fulfillment" (SH-S-7459); Salla's line is in its plan group order management (parent_code adar-altlbat), and Salla's shipments concern (SA-C-144, in CM-SHP-009) names tracking in Q1's name only. The customer notifications that carry a shipping update are D's CM-NTF-001.

capability: Delivery promises: the delivery promises the store makes, with their settings (Shopify delivery promises, delivery_promise_settings/update, shop-promise-examples; Salla Shipping Delivery Promises, delivery-promises)
note: Q1's M-049 (SH-C-125, SA-C-147). Shopify gives it a route of its own in section Shipping, shop-promise-examples, open to a beta (SH-S-7139, SH-S-5033), its scopes read_ and write_delivery_promises and the topic delivery_promise_settings/update; Salla its Merchant API folder Shipping Delivery Promises, beside Shipping Zones (SA-S-1052), and an unreleased flag delivery-promises (plans pro and special). Neither platform defines a delivery promise in what is held. Under CM-SHP-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's section Shipping, Salla's Merchant API folders of shipping. SA-C-147 lands in batch 12.

capability: Delivery option generators and shipping to pickup points: app-written functions that generate delivery options for checkout, among them pickup points and local pickup, and the admin's setting for shipping to pickup points (Shopify Pickup point delivery option generator, Local pickup delivery option generator, Fulfillment option generator, Shipping to pickup points)
note: Shopify gives it places of its own: the route pickup_points, titled Shipping to pickup points, in section Shipping (SH-S-7138), and the Function API targets local_pickup_delivery_option_generator and pickup_point_delivery_option_generator with the scope write_delivery_option_generators. Under CM-SHP-001 by that route's section. Nothing held defines a pickup point, or says whose location it is; the store's own pickup locations are CM-SHP-007. The function mechanism is F's CM-APP-005, as for CM-SHP-013 and CM-SHP-014.

capability: International shipping readiness and customs data: preparing products and shipments to be shipped abroad, with their customs code (HS code) and weight, and the platform's fee on international shipping (Salla International Shipping Readiness, international-product, كود التنسيق الجمركي للمنتج - HS code, رسوم بوابة الشحن الدولي; Shopify International shipping)
note: Salla gives it a place of its own: the admin link International Shipping Readiness at /shipping/international, in the same admin list as Shipping & delivery (SA-S-1873), with the released flag international-product. Under CM-SHP-001 by that path. Not CM-TAX-008 (duties and import taxes): SA-C-146's statements name a code that identifies shipments for export (SA-S-0167) and Salla's own service fee on international shipping (SA-S-0163), not duties or import taxes; the customs duties on Salla's labels (SA-S-5075) and the customs information field (SA-S-5074) stay in CM-TAX-008. Shopify's side is only its help-centre section International shipping (SH-I-2158).
